Michigan lost tough games against Iowa and Minnesota, but a gut-check win over Penn State threw the season a lifeline. Penn State tapped out long ago, Oregon isn't anything special, and Iowa and UCLA, while great, still have to survive the second half of the Big Ten season. The winner in Ann Arbor on Saturday has a chance to do some big things. Indiana vs Michigan: Quick Hits Michigan has winnable dates against Rutgers on the road before hosting Michigan State. And then comes the problem – at Oregon, UCLA, at Ohio State. The Hoosiers get three of their last four games at home, getting Minnesota and USC next. Indiana beat Michigan 20-15 in 2024. Before that, the Wolverines won 26 of the previous 27 games going back to 1987, with the lone loss in the shortened 2020 season. How To Watch Indiana vs Michigan Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, MI – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why Indiana Will Win It's crazy how this works. Had Nick Marsh been able to get one foot just a few inches over to one side, Indiana would be the unquestioned No. 1 team in both polls, and it would be ridiculous to give anyone else a single first-place vote. In other words, losing to Ohio State matters, of course, but … not really. The Hoosiers are still fantastic. Michigan still can't score. There were the 52 points hung up on UTEP, and last week's 21-18 win over Penn State was the only other time the offense scored more than 19 points. It's been a struggle, and the running game won't get better against the fourth-best run defense in America. Why Michigan Will Win Could Tommy Carr really be the answer? Yes, he's legendary Lloyd Carr's grandson, and yes, he's the younger brother of Notre Dame's CJ Carr, but he's at Michigan. The guy is talented. It's too easy to suggest that Bryce Underwood was the reason Michigan's offense was so bad, but he wasn't getting the job done – to be nice about it. All Carr did was hit 5-of-7 passes for 47 yards along with a rushing score. There's a new vibe now on offense, and … Indiana vs Michigan Prediction, Betting Lines It gets said every week, and it's important to keep bringing it up. The Michigan defense is fantastic. It's fourth in the nation overall, fantastic against the run, and it'll give the Indiana offense a whole slew of problems. The Wolverine running game still won't work, but Carr will be okay and the defense will keep this close until late. Like the Northwestern, Nebraska, and Ohio State games, though, Indiana will have to come up big in the fourth quarter. Like it did against the Wildcats and Huskers, it will. picks.headline: ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr
picks.blurb: ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr Isaiah Hole, Wolverines Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's going to be interesting this weekend when Michigan football hosts Indiana, given that the offense came alive with the quarterback switch from Bryce Underwood to Tommy Carr in the second half vs. Penn State . Given that the defense has been solid, if not elite (the Wolverines have the top-rated defense in yards per play), it should keep the game interesting, but if the offense can suddenly move? That could be a game-changer. On the ESPN College GameDay podcast on Wednesday, Dan Wetzel discussed the change, and noted that, in the wide-open Big Ten, the Wolverines aren't exactly out of it. "Michigan team that looked totally dead in the water until halftime of last week and may still be," Wetzel said. "But if Tommy Carr came in, they moved the offense -- he's still a true freshman, I'm not expecting a ton out of this, I don't expect this to happen. But if that sparks it -- there's no doubt that Michigan's got a defense, they've got some running backs. They could get this thing going and be at least a tough team to beat. Can spring some upsets, if not still -- conceivably, I mean, it's on the table and get to 10-2. So there's all sorts of different possibilities. And the Big Ten can make a really interesting race just in that league." That said, Wetzel does believe that the maize and blue will get their third loss this week with the Hoosiers coming to town. But, he does think that the game will be a bit closer than people would have thought just a few short weeks ago. "I'm intrigued as anything about what Michigan does at quarterback," Wetzel said. "Will both guys play: Underwood and Carr? Will they play both at the same time? You know, Utah, I said, Utah runs a two-quarterback system. That's where Whittingham came from. There was a definite spark and some competency and, like, reading run options and RPOs and different things, coming into a game and then starting a game or two different things. There's Whittingham trying to be coy about who's going to start. "How does Underwood respond to all of this? He was a very good teammate on the sideline. Does he come back if he gets back in the game and make some plays? So I'm very interested in what Michigan does. And I think they haven't been interesting all year because they haven't been able to do anything offensively, but I think they're interesting. "I think this is the worst possible opponent they could be playing is Indiana. They need a couple of turnovers. They need some penalties. They need a returned kick a bunch and keep this game low scoring to make it work. And I don't think Indiana is going to give them that. So I'll take the Hoosiers, but fascinating game for the Wolverines, no matter how the result ends up." Rece Davis agrees on all counts. But he thinks this could be a game where the maize and blue find at least some semblance of identity, but can't quite get over the hump of beating the defending national champion. "It's a great opportunity for Michigan, for sure," Davis said. "A great opportunity for Kyle Whittingham to sort of reestablish some confidence in the fan base, but the spot is wrong. The team is wrong that they're facing. I can't see Michigan with Tommy Carr or Bryce Underwood based on what we've seen from them offensively, doing enough to have a chance to win the game. They'll need some mistakes from Indiana. That's uncharacteristic. "I would assume even if Hoover isn't able to go full speed, they certainly don't have a guy that's experienced at Indiana, but I think their backup is Grant Wilson. I believe he's played, you know, he's an older guy. They'll have them coached up and ready. I think Indiana sort of methodically wins the game. I don't think they blow them out. It's going to be like a lot of the Michigan games we've seen and probably a lot like, maybe not quite as dramatic, but in final score, probably something somewhat similar to what we saw in Bloomington on Saturday between Indiana and Ohio State . I'll take the Hoosiers to roll." Michigan and Indiana kick off at 12:10 p.m. EDT, with the game set to be broadcast on Fox. away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

home.blurb: Michigan State, which was already severely shorthanded at linebacker and cornerback, listed starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic and starting running back Jaziun Patterson as questionable on Wednesday night. Coach Pat Fitzgerald has remained tight-lipped about injuries and there's still time before the Spartans arrive in Los Angeles but if both Milivojevic and Patterson are out, the team would be down to its No. 3 option at both quarterback and running back. The 11 players Michigan State listed out include lead linebacker Jordan Hall, four top cornerbacks (Tre Bell, Charles Brantley, Tyran Chappell and Keshawn Williams) and backup quarterback Cam Fancher. Wide receiver Charles Taplin, full back Jay Coyne, tight end Joe Caudill and offensive lineman Tristan Comer are also out. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:12 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, the SEC is up for grabs, and Auburn and LSU had a lot to do with that. Ten SEC teams fall into the 4-1 to 2-2 range after Auburn pulled off a stunning 27-24 win at Georgia last week. The rest of the AU Tiger schedule is challenging, but if you can beat Georgia in Sanford Stadium, the bar gets set a little higher. LSU lost both of its road games – Ole Miss and Kentucky – but it's been an unstoppable force at home, destroying Clemson by 41, Texas A&M by 29, and beating Mississippi State 31-0 last week. The Bayou Bengal Tigers are still among the most dangerous and talented teams in the country on the right day, but, like Auburn, one more loss and that's about it for the SEC and College Football Playoff dreams. LSU vs Auburn: Quick Hits LSU gets a nasty run over the next three games, but Alabama and Texas are home games before going to Tennessee. Auburn goes to Ole Miss next, and three of the last four SEC games are on the road. LSU beat Auburn 48-18 when the two last met in 2023 and has won six of the last eight games. How To Watch LSU vs Auburn Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn, AL – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why LSU Will Win LSU has to take the fight to Auburn right away, but without getting caught up in the tempo. The Auburn offense wants to move at a lightning-fast pace, and Lane Kiffin's attack is at its best when it's going 150 miles per hour. The one big difference is control of the tempo. LSU is amazing at dominating the time of possession battle, and it should hold the ball for large chunks of time. Auburn is 133rd in the nation, keeping the ball for fewer than 27 minutes per game. As much as the offense matters, though, it's the LSU defense that has to keep Auburn from getting out of third gear. LSU is second in the nation in sacks, and AU can't keep quarterback Byrum Brown from getting popped. Why Auburn Will Win It really is impressive. LSU looks and plays like it has 14 guys on the field who are all twice as fast as everyone else … at home. The LSU offense wasn't too bad in the losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky, but the defense occasionally played like it didn't attend the last three classes before the test. It's not a coincidence. LSU has allowed more than 145 passing yards just two times this season. Take a wild guess which teams got it going through the air. In case you were wondering, the 21-15 win over Vanderbilt is the only time Auburn failed to throw for at least 145 yards. LSU vs Auburn Prediction, Betting Lines Let's get it out of the way. It wasn't funny when the line was first written in 1999, and it's even more brutal now, but college football is nothing without its traditions, so … "This is our five-star, all-time, can't-miss lock of the century for this week … the Tigers are going to win." Really, how did Auburn beat Georgia? First of all, Auburn is just that good. But also, it actually held its own in the time of possession battle – the defense held up and wasn't gassed late. That, and it helped to get be +3 in turnover margin. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will throw his customary interception – although he didn't give one away for the first time all year in last week's win over Mississippi State – but LSU's control of the clock and the narrative on the lines will be enough to finally get a road win. away.blurb: LSU doesn’t list one of its stars in SEC availability report, signaling a possible return By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau LSU tight end Trey’Dez Green might be ready for a return this weekend. The Tigers’ preseason All-American was not listed on the Southeastern Conference’s initial availability report for the Auburn game, which is the first time Green hasn’t been listed as “out” since he was sidelined by a knee injury in a loss at Ole Miss in Week 3. LSU’s two other starters sidelined by long-term injuries, linebacker Whit Weeks and safety Dashawn Spears, were still listed as “out” Wednesday for the 11 a.m. Saturday kickoff. It was long believed Green could return after the open date next weekend, allowing him to play in a pivotal home game against Alabama on Nov. 7. But as LSU coach Lane Kiffin said on Oct. 5 before a trip to Kentucky, “If there's anybody that's going to come back sooner than maybe what people thought, it would be him.” Green was out of a knee brace at that time, and Kiffin said he was “getting closer.” Having him back to face Auburn is fortuitous, given the other Tigers just beat then-No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. LSU did list freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson as doubtful Wednesday for the road trip to Auburn. Reserve linebacker Tylen Singleton, who missed last weekend’s game against Mississippi State, was not listed and should be available. Kiffin said postgame Saturday that doctors held out both Umanmielen and receiver Jackson Harris, who appeared to injure his ankle on a second-half catch. Kiffin didn’t specify their injuries, but he said Sunday he believed Harris would be “fine.” “I feel like if the game went differently, I could have went back out there and played,” Harris told reporters. “So we'll be all good for this week.” Your browser is out of date and potentially vulnerable to security risks. Umanmielen exited LSU’s win over Mississippi State in the first quarter after a tackle. Green, the 6-foot-7, 237-pound junior, was having a breakout season before he took an Ole Miss helmet to the knee late in a 32-24 loss to the Rebels. He had 14 catches for 222 yards and a touchdown in three games. Harris, who has emerged as LSU’s leading receiver, confirmed as much Tuesday. away.headline: LSU football injury report | Star TE Trey'Dez Green off injury report
away.blurb: Star junior tight end Trey'Dez Green is no longer listed on the report released Wednesday, Oct. 21, signaling his possible return to the field for No. 17 LSU (5-2, 2-2 SEC). His removal from the injury report means Green (6-7, 240) will be available to play against Auburn (4-2, 2-2) inside Jordan-Hare Stadium Saturday (11 a.m. CT, ABC). Initially, his injury was feared to be worse than what it ended up being. But his possible return to action after just four weeks is quicker than it was projected. Two weeks ago, Kiffin said that Green was "getting closer" to returning. "If there's anybody that's going to come back sooner than maybe what people think, it would be him," Kiffin said. "He is out of the brace and moving it. So, getting closer." Freshman defensive lineman Richard Anderson is the new name to the injury report for LSU, and he is listed as doubtful. LSU has had rough injury luck this season with major key players getting hurt. Senior linebacker Whit Weeks fractured his fibula during the Texas A&M three weeks ago and his return to the field is uncertain. Junior safety Dashawn Spears suffered a season-ending knee injury in the Ole Miss game. LSU Tight End Trey’Dez Green Is Off SEC’s Injury Report For 1st Time Since Knee Injury At Ole Miss
away.blurb: The secret to LSU's first road win in the Southeastern Conference since 2024 may have just gotten out. Green, a giant 6-foot-7, 240-pound target for Leavitt, had been listed as “out” for LSU's last four games since injuring his knee as he was tackled early in the fourth quarter in the loss at Ole Miss on Sept. 19. Green caught four passes for 60 yards at Ole Miss. He has 14 catches for 222 yards and a touchdown in LSU's first three games. He is not even listed as “questionable” for this game, which means he is available to play at Auburn. LSU coach Lane Kiffin could keep Green out anyway, though, as he may be out of game shape and would have an open date next Saturday to get even healthier and more prepared as the Tigers do not play again after Auburn until Nov. 7 at home against Alabama. Green has been seen on the sidelines at LSU's last two games without the knee brace he previously wore after the injury. The only players listed as out for the Tigers are previously injured linebacker Whit Weeks (leg) and three players out for the season with injuries – defensive back Dashawn Spears, linebacker Charles Ross and wide receiver Phillip Wright III. For Auburn, backup offensive lineman Tai Buster and backup tight end Hunter Herring are both listed as out, while backup defensive tackle Saint Farrior is questionable. Starting linebacker Xavier Atkins is also out as he was dismissed from the team this week. home.headline: LSU football injury report puts Auburn's tackles under the gun
home.blurb: LSU will see EDGE Princewill Umanmielen's return to the field this coming Saturday after his name was not on the injury report for the Auburn game. Jacob Strand, who was formerly playing in the interior earlier this season, has gotten significant snaps at left tackle of late. He and Jo Simmons have a massive test this coming week against Umanmielen, who was previously questionable after missing most of the game against Mississippi State with an upper-body injury. We'll see if the Auburn offensive line is ready to protect quarterback Byrum Brown against it. Stanton Ramil graded out as an 80 on the right edge against Georgia in the epic Deep South's Oldest Rivalry upset . The interior held up remarkably well, with Wilson Zierer and Kenneth McManus taking starter snaps. Brown and Jeremiah Cobb showed out against the Dawgs with their best outings of the season. Auburn's run game could have a symbiotic effect with the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd and keep the pressure on LSU's defense. LSU football injury report puts Auburn's tackles under the gun Skip to main content About Alex Golesh, Joel Gordon, and Tyler Hudanick must now prepare for a physical freak with a 4.7-second 40-yard dash and an elite bend on Blake Baker's defense. The Ole Miss transfer Umanmielen immediately puts one of Golesh's recent big decisions to the test. Alex Golesh understands the challenge LSU is on the edge As Golesh said about LSU, "Those edges are real, like real real." Not only is Umanmielen a handful, but Tennessee transfer Jordan Ross is also elite. Ross had six tackles and a sack against State this past Saturday. Ross has three sacks this year, which ranks third behind defensive tackle Deuce Geralds's five and Umanmielen's eight. The group is even playing without Gabriel Reliford, who tore his ACL in the spring. The roster Lane Kiffin recruited has an embarrassment of riches in Baton Rouge. Auburn's run game has breakout chance against LSU Umanmielen isn't as renowned against the run. With that said, LSU's defense is better overall against the run than the pass. If you're looking for ways to nab an upset on Saturday and prove the Plains is haunted for favored opponents , controlling the clock is one of the most obvious. Brown is the ultimate wild card for Auburn. If he can keep LSU's defense guessing, opening up running lanes in the middle for Auburn when LSU's linebackers drop into coverage, perhaps Cobb, Omar Mabson, and the rest of the running backs could be difference-makers in a pivotal SEC clash.

picks.headline: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. By Parker Gillam Published: Oct 21, 2026 · 7:58 PM EDT Tennessee is set to pay a visit to South Carolina this Saturday, and the Volunteers are still riding high following their upset win over Alabama last weekend. But Columbia has been far from kind to the Volunteers in recent memory, as they've dropped 6 of their last 8 contests at Williams-Brice Stadium heading into this one. That was one of the many points ESPN's Greg McElroy made in his breakdown of the game during an episode of his “Always College Football” show, and the former Alabama quarterback is actually picking the Gamecocks to pull off the upset. “I'm gonna take South Carolina to win this game, 27-24, and I think they're gonna do it on the ground,” McElroy said . “They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war, and looked amazing doing it. picks.headline: Can Tennessee football maintain momentum at South Carolina? Our pick
picks.blurb: How I rank Tennessee football's five remaining opponents | Adams News Sports Business Go Knoxville Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Can Tennessee football maintain momentum at South Carolina? Our pick Emmett Siegel Knoxville News Sentinel Oct. 22, 2026, 5:07 a.m. ET The No. 11 Tennessee Volunteers will face the South Carolina Gamecocks on October 24. South Carolina is looking to build on a recent win against Florida after a slow start to their season. Key players for the Gamecocks include quarterback LaNorris Sellers and edge rusher Dylan Stewart. Tennessee's defense has been dominant this season, leading the SEC in several key statistical categories. Tennessee football is tasked with avoiding a letdown after a convincing win against Alabama, and it'll have to do so in a hostile road environment. The No. 11 Vols (6-1, 3-1 SEC) play South Carolina (3-3, 1-3) at Williams-Brice Stadium on Oct. 24 (3:30 p.m., ESPN). Tennessee's last trip to Columbia in 2022 ended with a blowout loss that knocked it out of College Football Playoff contention. It'll try to avoid a similar fate this year and maintain its footing in the CFP race before its open week. Here's what to know about the matchup. South Carolina's season started slow before Florida win Just a few weeks ago, it looked as though South Carolina's season was hanging on by a thread. The Gamecocks started 0-3 in SEC play. After a 4-8 season last year, coach Shane Beamer's seat was getting scorching hot. But they bought themselves a bit more time with a 38-19 win at Florida before the open week. And while the game before that was a home loss to Kentucky, South Carolina was one two-point conversion stop away from winning in overtime. Beamer still needs a decent finish to quiet discussions about his job security, but his team has shown it is capable of beating just about anyone in the SEC. In 2024, with many of the same key players, the Gamecocks went 9-4 and nearly made the CFP. LaNorris Sellers, Dylan Stewart star at premium positions South Carolina has game changers at premium positions on both offense and defense with quarterback LaNorris Sellers and edge rusher Dylan Stewart. When Sellers is on his game he is one of the best quarterbacks in the SEC, but he's been glaringly inconsistent. He had turnover problems in losses to Alabama and Mississippi State and was at that point tied for the second-worst completion rate in the SEC (62.1%). The next week he threw for 226 yards and two touchdowns with 147 rushing yards against Kentucky. Stewart has also had a season of ups and downs. He is a likely top-10 pick the 2027 NFL Draft but missed three of the first five games of this season, one because of a suspension after he punched an Alabama player in the helmet. Then he came back against Florida and dominated with two forced fumbles and a sack. If Sellers and Stewart are at their best, South Carolina can beat any team it plays. Tennessee's defense has been elite Few defenses in the country are as well-equipped as Tennessee's to handle a mobile quarterback like Sellers. The Vols rank first in the SEC in sacks, explosive plays allowed, tackles for loss, scoring defense, opposing passer rating and fourth-down defense. Defensive coordinator Jim Knowles' unit has been nothing short of dominant through seven games. The Vols have also forced multiple turnovers in three of their last four games, including four against Alabama. South Carolina lost the turnover battle in its first three SEC games and lost them all. When it was plus-three against Florida, it won by multiple scores. Tennessee vs South Carolina prediction Tennessee 24, South Carolina 21: This is a major trap game for Tennessee on the road after an emotional win, but its defense should travel just fine. The matchup may be decided by who's better between Vols running back DeSean Bishop and the Gamecocks' run defense that ranks third in the SEC. Oddsmakers slightly favor South Carolina in a spot that feels ripe for an unranked-over-ranked result. Still, picking against Tennessee's defense has been a fool's errand. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. “Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?” said McElroy. “Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. “I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. There's a big gap between Miami and the rest of the ACC, but here is where Clemson and all 17 conference teams rank in ESPN's FPI: 17. Stanford Cardinal (-11.4 FPI) 16. Florida State Seminoles (9.6 FPI) 4. SMU Mustangs (9.8 FPI) 3. Louisville Cardinals (13.3 FPI) 2. Wake Forest Demon Deacons (15.4 FPI) 1. Miami Hurricanes (26.5 FPI) What are ESPN FPI ratings? ESPN explains: "The Football Power Index (FPI) is a measure of team strength that is meant to be the best predictor of a team's performance going forward for the rest of the season. FPI represents how many points above or below average a team is. Projected results are based on 20,000 simulations of the rest of the season using FPI, results to date, and the remaining schedule. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." picks.blurb: That's the mantra of Clemson coach Dabo Swinney , whose teams sits at 4-2 and 2-1 in the ACC. The Tigers host the Virginia Tech Hokies (5-2, 2-2) in a critical prime-time matchup in Week 8 at Clemson Memorial Stadium. Clemson defeated Charleston Southern, 37-0, in Week 7 behind a defense that yielded only 76 yards of total offense and a rushing attack that ran for 231 yards. Chris Johnson Jr. had two touchdowns, and Gideon Davidson led the Tigers' ground game with 59 yards on 13 carries. Tigers receivers hurt themselves with some costly drops in the game, which is something Swinney has repeatedly highlighted this week . Quarterback Tait Reynolds finished 17 of 26 for 127 passing yards in the true freshman's fourth start at quarterback. Virginia Tech is coming off a 34-24 win over Georgia Tech in Blacksburg. Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns in the win. He leads the ACC in passing yards with 1,984 through seven games. Hokies leading rusher Jeffrey Overton is averaging six yards per carry. Coach James Franklin's team ranks 28th nationally in total offense, good for sixth in the ACC. The Hokies are 32nd nationally in total defense, fifth-best in the conference. Clemson is 110th nationally in total offense with 340.7 yards per game, second to last among ACC teams and ahead of only North Carolina. The Tigers are 46th nationally in total defense, which ranks 10th in the ACC. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Virginia Tech, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Hokies winning by three points, which goes against oddsmakers' 2.5 spread favoring the Tigers. Connelly's final score prediction: Virginia Tech 26, Clemson 23. He gives the Hokies a win probability of 56%. Where Clemson football sits in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 8 Clemson is No. 56 in the ESPN SP+ team rankings , up five spots from last week. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.0, up from 2.2 a week ago. Clemson is one spot below ACC rival Florida State (4.9) and one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.1 rating on offense (No. 98 nationally, down one spot from last week) and a 19.5 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is up five spots from before the Tigers' win over Charleston Southern. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.3 rating, which ranks 20th in the nation. Virginia Tech is No. 40 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 8.9, one spot below the Oregon State Beavers and one spot ahead of the Baylor Bears. The metrics give the Hokies a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 36 nationally, a 23.4 rating on defense that's No. 43 in the nation, and a minus-0.3 rating in special teams (No. 112). What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night's game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

away.headline: Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets?
away.blurb: The Yellow Jackets are going to be trying to pull off an upset against the Hokies today, but they are going to have to do so with some key players out. The final availability report is out for this game, and it includes the final status for running back Justice Haynes, who was listed as doubtful coming into Saturday, as well as offensive lineman Josh Petty and defensive lineman Landen Marshall. RB Justice Haynes and OT Josh Petty are going to be game-time decisions. If Haynes is unable to go today, Trelain Maddox and Chad Alexander would be the top options in the backfield for the Yellow Jackets today against Virginia Tech. Maddox is coming off the best game of his career last week against Duke. Riggs, the Yellow Jackets starting center, came back from an injury last week in the win over Duke, but was hurt during the game and did not return. He was not on the injury report this week and should be starting in the middle of the Yellow Jackets offensive line against what has been one of the ACC's best defensive fronts through the first part of the season. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/georgiatech as Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets? . Kickoff time is getting closer for Georgia Tech and Virginia Tech. How do these injuries impact Georgia Tech today? There are two notable names not on the injury report this week and those are Jameson Riggs and Noah Carter. Carter has been perhaps the Yellow Jackets' most consistent pass rusher (although the pass rush has not been very good), and without Walker, Boyd, or Hoffler to get after the quarterback, Carter is going to be relied on to put pressure on Hokies QB Ethan Grunkemeyer, and Virginia Tech's offensive line has not been one of the best in the ACC so far this season. As poorly as the season started for Georgia Tech, a win on the road against the Hokies would be something that could potentially start to turn their season around. The Yellow Jackets have only one conference loss and with the ACC looking wide open after Miami, Georgia Tech can star to build some momentum that could get them to their fourth consecutive bowl appearance under Brent Key. Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech
home.blurb: Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech Skip to main content SI.COM "Well, he had his best day yesterday, but he's gonna be out this weekend," he said. "He's got a concussion, so he'll be out unfortunately. But he had a great day; had a couple of good catches." "I thought, Gordo was a guy that came out of spring ball that I thought, 'Here we go,' and he dealt with some injuries in fall camp, and it kind of set him back," Morris said on Wednesday. "It was really good to see his speed. I thought he flashed." "You know, he's really kind of been that next guy, and that's really been since the spring," he finished. "He just kind of emerged, and then he pulled his hamstring in camp and has kind of been limited a good bit, but has been able to play some and kind of been working his way back." As it stands, there's no clear timetable for Sellars' return, but true freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds will still have plenty of weapons in the Week 8 conference matchup, with Bryant Wesco Jr. and T.J. Moore ready to get back on track. As the Clemson Tigers head back into ACC play against Virginia Tech this weekend, they'll be without a key depth piece on the offensive side of the ball. Speaking during media availability on Wednesday, head coach Dabo Swinney announced that true freshman wideout Gordon Sellars III will miss the Week 8 contest vs. the Hokies due to a concussion he suffered in practice on Tuesday. As we reported earlier this season, Sellars has been a standout , not just among the freshmen but among the receivers as a whole, taking over as the primary backup on the outside while sophomore Juju Preston fills the backup slot role. It's an untimely setback for a freshman who has been trending up, and one that offensive coordinator Chad Morris says he saw coming back during the spring period. Swinney shared a similar view, and the concussion is especially frustrating for a young talent who worked hard to come back from the hamstring injury Morris referenced during fall camp. Not to mention, junior tight end Christian Bentancur is coming off a career-high four catches for 74 yards against Charleston Southern in Week 7. So we'll see if Morris continues to open up the playbook for pass-catching outside of receivers. Swinney and the Tigers are set to kick off from Memorial Stadium at 7 p.m. ET, and the game will be broadcast on ESPN. picks.headline: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch
picks.blurb: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning warms up before a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. © Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Prateek Singh Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:41 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Arch Manning's struggles against the Florida Gators have put the Texas Longhorns in a difficult position ahead of their matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday. Manning threw for 173 yards, completed 14 of 20 passes, and threw one touchdown. According to former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel, Texas will need to make key adjustments to its strategy ahead of the upcoming game. During an appearance on CBS Sports, Neuheisel picked Ole Miss to win. "I'm concerned for Texas in this game, not because I don't think they'll play hard and be geared up to play their best game of the season, but I feel like because of all the pressure on Arch, they're going to condense, and condensing will not be the answer to going against Pete Golding defense," he said . Neuheisel pointed out that Arch Manning attempted just 20 passes against Florida, arguing that such an approach will not be effective against the Ole Miss Rebels. While the Texas Longhorns have won four of their six games this season, Manning has shown only flashes of brilliance rather than the consistency expected of him. Overall, Manning has completed 106 of 166 passes for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns, and five interceptions. After his performance against the Gators, speculation began that he could be benched for the upcoming game. However, head coach Steve Sarkisian made it clear that Arch Manning will remain the team's starting quarterback. "There's no doubt about it, Arch can play better for us, but he's our starter," he said , per Fox Sports. "We need to see a better version of him this week." Sarkisian said Manning is a quality player and that, as a coach, it is his job to bring out the best in him on the field. Former Texas Coach Heaps Praise on Arch Manning On an episode of THE STAMPEDE, former Texas coach Mack Brown said Arch Manning and the rest of the Longhorns are playing under immense pressure. He believes the team needs to free itself from that pressure before stepping onto the field. In Brown's view, Manning has the talent and ability to help get Texas back on track. "Arch's gotta go back and be the Arch we saw at the last of last year," he said. "He's good enough, he's athletic enough, he's smart enough, and for a 22-year-old, he has handled this pressure so well." Brown said the upcoming matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels will be crucial for the Longhorns and could shape their chances of making the College Football Playoff this season. picks.headline: Expert CFB Locks, Predictions for Ole Miss vs. Texas and Week 8's Biggest Games
picks.blurb: College Football Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College Football If not for one single step, last week's picks would have been dominant. But college football sometimes works like that. One minute you're breaking free of the defensive back, eyeing a walk-off win in one of the biggest games of the year. The next, your foot inexplicably lands out of bounds, and everything goes up in flames. It was that close for Indiana last week against Ohio State. We were also that close to a 7-2 week, although 6-3 will do just fine. As for Week 8, consider us intrigued. It doesn't have the same buffet of massive matchups on paper, although those are normally the weeks that deliver. After such a bananas Saturday, maybe it's just going to be one of those seasons. Here's to hoping. As for another week of winners, here they are. Last Week's Record: 6-3 Year to Date: 33-33-1 All point spreads courtesy of FanDuel Texas (-3) vs. Ole Miss Tim Warner/Getty Images Oh, it's a mess in Austin. Let's not paint this picture any differently. Following an emphatic come-from-behind win over Ohio State, Texas played a lackluster game against UTSA and followed it up with two ugly losses to Oklahoma and Florida. Steve Sarkisian spent a week defending Arch Manning; now he's giving backup quarterback KJ Lacey Jr., who has thrown a grand total of nine passes across his two seasons with the program, more reps. Despite the losses and the drama, Texas is favored over a team coming off (arguably) its best win all season. Ole Miss clobbered Missouri, which was playing fantastic football coming into last week. Perhaps most importantly, the Rebels limited the Mizzou offense to just three points. So, why do this? Why should we back a team in disarray despite all the recent data points? Beyond our general contrarian style, Ole Miss didn't exactly dazzle in its only true road test thus far against Florida, allowing the Gators to rack up nearly 500 yards of offense. While the Longhorns have issues in all facets, playing on the road in this conference is never easy. Texas, questions aplenty, finds a way. The Pick: Texas (-3) South Carolina (-2.5) vs. Tennessee James Gilbert/Getty Images From one fascinating point spread in the SEC to another, enter South Carolina-Tennessee. The Vols, currently. No. 11 in the AP Poll, coming off a dominant win over Alabama, are underdogs to a three-win team that suffered an ugly three-game losing streak earlier in the year. Such is life in the SEC. For Tennessee, what a performance from the defense. The Vols' D limited Alabama to just 201 yards of offense and forced four turnovers. Tennessee is currently No. 9 in scoring defense and first in the nation in sacks. The issue, however, is that the offense never looked quite right. QB George MacIntyre wasn't superb, but he did enough. While we might not know the starter until game day, it seems likely that MacIntyre will get the nod over Faizon Brandon. For South Carolina, it probably won't matter. In dire need of a win, the Gamecocks absolutely clobbered Florida in their last game before enjoying a bye in Week 7. LaNorris Sellers had arguably his best collegiate game to date. Dylan Stewart was back and all over the place. All was right for one week. Now, South Carolina will play at home against a team with massive hangover potential. The timing is right. The Pick: South Carolina (-2.5) Wisconsin (+3) vs. USC Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For Wisconsin, Week 7 was a missed opportunity. There's no other way to shape it. UCLA deserves credit for beating the Badgers with a backup QB, although Wisconsin had plenty of chances to win. Completing just six passes and throwing for 66 yards doesn't help. Despite the lack of offense, the oddsmakers see this as a tight game. USC, which enjoyed a bye last week, comes into Week 8 with a solid 6-1 mark. However, the reality behind those numbers tells a different story. USC played an ugly football game against Rutgers, lost to Oregon without its starting QB and nearly lost to Washington and Penn State. Lincoln Riley deserves credit for finding a way to win those games. That's one way to look at it. Another is that the Trojans are due for a slip-up. This feels like a moment that fits that outcome perfectly. Wisconsin must find a way to get quarterback Colton Joseph into a better rhythm. He should find success on the ground; that's the norm. But getting more comfortable as a passer should be the goal. Defensively, Wisconsin should slow USC's offense. If the Wisconsin offense can do enough, don't be shocked if the Badgers win outright. The Pick: Wisconsin (+3) Week 8 CFB Picks 🔮 Latest College Football Odds and Picks Factoring in New Weather Forecasts for Week 8 Schedule B/R's Expert Week 7 2026 NFL Picks UCF (+6.5) vs. BYU Brian Bahr/Getty Images Well, we know how the public will bet this one. Coming off an enormous win over Notre Dame, BYU, which is now No. 2 in the AP Poll, is laying less than a touchdown against an unranked team with a .500 record. The masses will flock to bet BYU. In many ways, it makes sense. Quarterback Bear Bachmeier is excellent. BYU's defense just played a largely brilliant game. There's a lot to like about this program, as the development under Kalani Sitake is undeniable. But let's make sure our memories aren't short. This same BYU team struggled on the road against TCU and wasn't exactly dominant against Iowa State. That's not meant to take anything away from their efforts. It simply points out that these opponents have delivered close games before. While the Cougars will travel after an emphatic win, UCF enjoyed a bye after two consecutive losses on the road. Quarterback Keyone Jenkins has played well while filling in for starter Alonza Barnett III. He'll start again. At home, this team looks like it could push the No. 2 team to the brink. The oddsmakers feel that way, and so do we. The Pick: UCF (+6.5) Michigan (+7) vs. Indiana Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images Football hangovers work in mysterious ways, and we're about to find out exactly how Indiana responds after suffering a loss—something it hasn't done in quite some time. And it wasn't just any loss; this was a heartbreaker. Yes, Indiana could have beaten Ohio State if not for the play we alluded to at the very start. But to summarize the Hoosiers' performance on this play alone would be a mistake. Indiana's offense looked out of sync, Josh Hoover missed a lot of easy throws and the Hoosiers' running game averaged just two-and-a-half yards per carry, albeit against a quality opponent and defense. Michigan, meanwhile, has new life. Quarterback Bryce Underwood was benched for freshman Tommy Carr, grandson of Michigan legend Lloyd Carr. After entering the game, Carr led the Wolverines to a key win over Penn State. While head coach Kyle Whittingham didn't officially name Carr the starter, it feels like a formality. In terms of energy, this game features one team riding the high of its new starting QB playing at home. The other is trying to shake off the emotions of a really difficult loss. Indiana wins. Michigan keeps it tight. The Pick: Michigan (+7) Other Games on the Card Zach Del Bello/Getty Images Memphis (-10) vs. East Carolina The Tigers turned the ball over six times in an ugly loss against Tulane. They were still in the game for a while. Playing at home as a double-digit favorite should be exactly what this team needs. TCU (-9.5) vs. West Virginia Another sizable chalk, which feels somewhat noteworthy, given West Virginia's Week 7 win over Cincinnati at home. The Mountaineers won for us last week, although we still have serious concerns about that defense. Kansas (+3) vs Baylor The Baylor offense mustered just six points last week against TCU. The Bears are just a short favorite over a two-win team. It goes without saying, but Kansas could use this one badly. Nevada (-5.5) vs. San Jose State On the topic of backing two-win teams, enter Nevada. The schedule hasn't exactly been favorable of late, which is at least partly to blame. picks.blurb: my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores SPORTS & TEAMS PERSONALITIES POPULAR SEARCHES College Football Add FOX Sports on Google College Football Week 8 Expert Picks, Predictions For Texas-Ole Miss And More Published Oct. 22, 2026 7:00 a.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Week 7 of the college football season was chaotic, with five of the top seven teams falling. The upsets confounded experts everywhere, but they'll try to rebound in Week 8. It starts with "Big Noon Kickoff" as No. 6 Indiana tries to bounce back from its loss to No. 3 Ohio State against a Michigan team, resurging after a quarterback change. Arch Manning will try to keep his job as he leads No. 19 Texas into a must-win game against No. 7 Ole Miss. Then the night ends with a Big 12 matchup with College Football Playoff stakes when undefeated No. 10 Utah hosts No. 14 Houston. After consecutive weeks where the No. 1 team lost, the field is wide open. Weâre breaking down our straight-up picks and the matchups to watch closely throughout the weekend. Michigan vs. No. 6 Indiana Curt Cignetti and Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end when the Hoosiers were defeated by Ohio State in Week 7. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (FOX) Where: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, Michigan Line: Indiana -7 RJ Young: Indiana After watching Indiana's defense turn Julian Sayin into a tackling dummy, I shudder to think what it might do against Michigan's newly named starting quarterback, Tommy Carr. Laken Litman: Indiana The Hoosiers have never lost back to back games under Curt Cignetti and that won't start now â not even with Michigan likely starting Tommy Carr at quarterback. Ben Portnoy: Indiana After being in Bloomington last week for Indiana's loss to Ohio State, I think I'm more confident than ever that the Hoosiers can repeat as Big Ten champions. Michigan should get a nice spark from Tommy Carr, but I'm skeptical of a first-time starter against Bryant Haines' defense. No. 1 Miami vs. Pitt Quarterback Darian Mensah kept Miami's undefeated season alive with multiple clutch drives against Florida State. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (ESPN) Where: Hard Rock Stadium, Miami, Florida Line: Miami -20.5 Young: Miami The No. 1 team in the country needs to act like it against a team that lost its star player and starting quarterback Mason Heintschel earlier this season. Litman: Miami The 'Canes escaped their scariest test of the season vs. Florida State last week and will be locked in against a struggling Pitt team. Portnoy: Miami Pitt hasn't been the same team since Mason Heintschel was lost for the season. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is still my pick for the Heisman Trophy and I think he'll put up more big numbers on Saturday. No. 18 LSU vs. Auburn Alex Golesh led Auburn to an upset over top-ranked Georgia in Week 7, the first time the Tigers have defeated the No. 1 ranked team since 2017. (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (ABC) Where: Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn, Alabama Line: LSU -7.5 Young: LSU I sincerely doubt Auburn can pull off that trick of knocking off a top-25 team for the second week in a row. Litman: Auburn Jordan-Hare Stadium will be rocking and ready for Auburn to upset its second straight SEC powerhouse. Portnoy: LSU The Tigers are in do-or-die mode right now. LSU brass spent millions to flip this roster and bring Lane Kiffin to Baton Rouge. I think it keeps its CFP hopes â fleeting as they may be â alive for one more week. UCF vs. No. 2 BYU BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw for one touchdown and rushed for two more in the Cougars' upset of Notre Dame in Week 7. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FOX) Where: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, Florida Line: BYU -6.5 Young: BYU I don't believe in "emotional letdowns," and UCF has been playing without star quarterback Alonza Barnett III most of this season. Litman: BYU The Cougars don't seem like the kind of team that's going to have a letdown week after their massive win over Notre Dame. How many ways will quarterback Bear Bachmeier score this Saturday? Portnoy: BYU No Alonza Barnett III, no way UCF is winning this game. The Golden Knights are improved in Year 2 of the Scott Frost Era (Part 2), but the Cougars look like the best team in the Big 12. I think they get it done, even in a potential letdown spot here. South Carolina vs. No. 11 Tennessee Josh Heupel improved to 2-1 against Kalen DeBoer. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (ESPN) Where: Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia, South Carolina Line: South Carolina -2.5 Young: Tennessee With George MacIntyre at quarterback and DeSean Bishop as the engine powering the Power T offense, the Volunteers look a lot like the 2024 version that made the College Football Playoff. Litman: Tennessee It's never easy to win on the road in the SEC, but Tennessee ekes this one out against a rejuvenated South Carolina team coming off a bye. Portnoy: South Carolina Tennessee smoked Alabama last week, but I'm still not sure how good the Volunteers are. Williams-Brice has a tendency to bring weird results (See the 2022 meeting between these two teams for proof of as much). I'll take Shane Beamer to further cool his hot seat. Minnesota vs. No. 15 Iowa Minnesota is 1-8 against Iowa under P.J. Fleck. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FS1) Where: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, Minnesota Line: Iowa -6.5 Young: Iowa The Hawkeyes play a better version of smashmouth football offensively than the Golden Gophers do. Litman: Iowa The Hawkeyes continue their journey to a CFP berth in what's become a wide open Big Ten. Portnoy: Iowa The Hawkeyes may have a quarterback decision to be made between Jeremy Hecklinski and Hank Brown, but they might finally have figured out the offense. Give me Kirk Ferentz's bunch in this one. No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss Trinidad Chambliss threw for three touchdowns and ran for one more in Ole Miss' win against Missouri in Week 8. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC) Where: DKR-Memorial Stadium, Austin, Texas Line: Texas -3 Young: Ole Miss Texas is one loss away from folding this season. The Rebels look like a team that could find their way into the SEC Championship Game Litman: Ole Miss The Rebels will not miss this opportunity to beat a conference opponent when they're already down. Portnoy: Ole Miss Texas is in free-fall mode and there's nothing I've seen from Arch Manning this year that makes me think he can win a quarterback duel with Trinidad Chambliss. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC) Where: Camp Randall Stadium, Austin, Texas Line: USC -3 Young: USC The Trojans are more talented offensively than Wisconsin. Litman: USC Head coach Lincoln Riley gets another Big Ten road win and keeps his team from looking ahead to next week's showdown vs. Ohio State. Portnoy: USC Lincoln Riley has quietly built a bit of stability in recent weeks. A win over Wisconsin would go a long way before a Julian Sayin-less, uber-talented Ohio State team comes to L.A. next week. Lobos get it done against the efficiency machine that is North Dakota State. This, and Utah nearly dropped last week's game to a two-win Colorado. Litman: Houston This is a tough one, but the Cougars get a massive win on the road behind sneaky Heisman Trophy candidate quarterback Conner Weigman. Portnoy: Houston Utah hasn't had a chance to prove itself yet, but I've liked what I've seen from the Houston offense and Texas A&M reclamation project Conner Weigman. Willie Fritz has the Cougars riding high after last week's huge victory over Oklahoma State. That momentum carries them in this one. away.headline: Texas releases injury report for Ole Miss matchup
away.blurb: Texas star edge Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for Saturday’s matchup after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the loss to Florida, while running back Hollywood Smothers is listed as questionable. Smothers reportedly missed practice on Monday due to a shoulder injury. Other names listed for the Longhorns are wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman (both questionable), as well as freshman edge Richard Wesley (out). Simmons going down during the Florida game is a huge blow for the Texas defense, as he has been playing at an extremely high level. Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp is going to need all hands on deck on Saturday to defend Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who has been one of the most dynamic playmakers in the country at the quarterback position, especially with the surprise news that Wesley is out. On top of that, Ole Miss will likely have star running back Kewan Lacy back on the field, as he is listed as probable on tonight’s injury report. The initial SEC injury report was released for the Saturday matchup between the No. 19 Texas Longhorns and against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on Wednesday and while the Rebels have many more players on their side of the injury report, there are certainly some notable names for the Longhorns as well. Every game moving forward is a must-win for the Longhorns after dropping the last two matchups. They will need to get healthy moving forward as they try to navigate a difficult stretch in the schedule with eight straight games to close the season.

away.headline: Colin Simmons ruled doubtful for Ole Miss game in first Texas injury report
away.blurb: Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for the upcoming SEC contest at Royal-Memorial Stadium. Simmons exited last week's 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators early in the fourth quarter due to a right-leg injury, and he did not return to the game. Simmons will look to continue his climb up two all-time Texas leaderboards upon his potential return to the field this week/later this season. Simmons raised his career sack total to 31 1/2 in the loss to Florida, moving him to No. 3 on Texas' all-time leaderboard (and nine sacks behind Kiki DeAyala's program-record 40.5 sacks). Simmons also has DeAyala's single-season record in his sights. Simmons exited the weekend with 10 1/2 sacks in 2026, 12 sacks behind DeAyala's record-setting 22 1/2-sack season in 1982. Texas will face perhaps college football's best quarterback Saturday when Ole Miss ' Trinidad Chambliss comes to Austin. The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) will likely do so without their best defensive player. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Saturday he believed Simmons suffered a right-knee injury against Florida, but was unaware of the injury's severity. Sarkisian didn't elaborate on Simmons' injury Monday, but Orangeblood's Anwar Richardson reported Simmons will miss three-to-four weeks due to a high-ankle sprain. Simmons' exit against Florida halted his statistical climb and hindered the Longhorns defense. Texas will likely now be without Simmons against Ole Miss and Chambliss, a scary situation after back-to-back SEC losses. Read this story on statesman.com

away.headline: Kewan Lacy's Texas Homecoming Comes With an Injury Question for Ole Miss
away.blurb: "So I think every week is going to be pretty similar with him. I mean, you’ve got an experienced player that’s been in the system, right? So, you know, our responsibility throughout the week is to make sure we’re protecting him and taking care of him," Golding said on Monday. "It’s not like he’s forgot how to play football. So obviously the game plan is going to change a little bit week in and week out...But as far as, you know, the physicality of having to run the football, you know, versus scout team and all that, it’s not that..." For the second straight week, Kewan Lacy returns to familiar grounds. Last week, Lacy finished with 122 rushing yards against his former team, the Missouri Tigers. This week, Lacy returns to his home state of Texas. The Ole Miss running back attended Lancaster High School, located just outside of downtown Dallas. Lacy grew up a Texas Longhorns fan, and he'll have a chance to play against his childhood team, but his availability comes with caution. Keeping Lacy Healthy is a Top Priority Lacy has battled injuries all season. He missed one game with a shoulder injury, but even when Lacy was on the field, Rebels fans hadn't seen the star running back fully unlocked until Saturday. Lacy looked like his 2025 self against the Tigers. Lacy and Ole Miss would love to build on that momentum against Texas. But Pete Golding is remaining cautious with Lacy and his workload throughout the week. Lacy handled 306 carries last season. The Rebels leaned on him more than they'd like, so the coaching staff appears much more cautious with Lacy this season. He'll likely take it easy during practice and he'll be ramped up on gameday. This year, Ole Miss has someone who can take pressure off Lacy. Makhi Frazier is averaging 5.6 yards per carry on 45 attempts. Frazier's running ability makes life easier for Lacy and gives opposing defenses a different look at running back. As mentioned earlier, Lacy returns to the school he grew up watching. During SEC Media Days, Lacy said he wanted to commit to Texas, but the Longhorns never gave him an opportunity. Now, he'll be on the opposing side with his family in the crowd. “It’s going to mean a lot, just coming back home. I don’t really hold anything against Texas," Lacy said. "But it’s a hometown game, so I’m excited to have all my family, friends there.” If the Rebels are going to pull off a massive road victory, they'll need Lacy to have another dominant game. The junior defensive standout required assistance leaving the field before eventually being transported to the locker room on a cart. Before exiting, Simmons had delivered another impressive performance, recording eight tackles, four tackles for loss and one sack. His absence represents a substantial blow to a Texas defense that has relied heavily on his ability to disrupt opposing offenses. Through six games, Simmons has recorded 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss, leading the nation in both categories. home.headline: Colin Simmons ruled doubtful for Ole Miss game in first Texas injury report
home.blurb: Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for the upcoming SEC contest at Royal-Memorial Stadium. Simmons exited last week's 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators early in the fourth quarter due to a right-leg injury, and he did not return to the game. Simmons will look to continue his climb up two all-time Texas leaderboards upon his potential return to the field this week/later this season. Simmons raised his career sack total to 31 1/2 in the loss to Florida, moving him to No. 3 on Texas' all-time leaderboard (and nine sacks behind Kiki DeAyala's program-record 40.5 sacks). Simmons also has DeAyala's single-season record in his sights. Simmons exited the weekend with 10 1/2 sacks in 2026, 12 sacks behind DeAyala's record-setting 22 1/2-sack season in 1982. Texas will face perhaps college football's best quarterback Saturday when Ole Miss ' Trinidad Chambliss comes to Austin. The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) will likely do so without their best defensive player. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Saturday he believed Simmons suffered a right-knee injury against Florida, but was unaware of the injury's severity. Sarkisian didn't elaborate on Simmons' injury Monday, but Orangeblood's Anwar Richardson reported Simmons will miss three-to-four weeks due to a high-ankle sprain. Simmons' exit against Florida halted his statistical climb and hindered the Longhorns defense. Texas will likely now be without Simmons against Ole Miss and Chambliss, a scary situation after back-to-back SEC losses. Read this story on statesman.com
