home.headline: Kewan Lacy's Texas Homecoming Comes With an Injury Question for Ole Miss
home.blurb: "So I think every week is going to be pretty similar with him. I mean, you’ve got an experienced player that’s been in the system, right? So, you know, our responsibility throughout the week is to make sure we’re protecting him and taking care of him," Golding said on Monday. "It’s not like he’s forgot how to play football. So obviously the game plan is going to change a little bit week in and week out...But as far as, you know, the physicality of having to run the football, you know, versus scout team and all that, it’s not that..." For the second straight week, Kewan Lacy returns to familiar grounds. Last week, Lacy finished with 122 rushing yards against his former team, the Missouri Tigers. This week, Lacy returns to his home state of Texas. The Ole Miss running back attended Lancaster High School, located just outside of downtown Dallas. Lacy grew up a Texas Longhorns fan, and he'll have a chance to play against his childhood team, but his availability comes with caution. Keeping Lacy Healthy is a Top Priority Lacy has battled injuries all season. He missed one game with a shoulder injury, but even when Lacy was on the field, Rebels fans hadn't seen the star running back fully unlocked until Saturday. Lacy looked like his 2025 self against the Tigers. Lacy and Ole Miss would love to build on that momentum against Texas. But Pete Golding is remaining cautious with Lacy and his workload throughout the week. Lacy handled 306 carries last season. The Rebels leaned on him more than they'd like, so the coaching staff appears much more cautious with Lacy this season. He'll likely take it easy during practice and he'll be ramped up on gameday. This year, Ole Miss has someone who can take pressure off Lacy. Makhi Frazier is averaging 5.6 yards per carry on 45 attempts. Frazier's running ability makes life easier for Lacy and gives opposing defenses a different look at running back. As mentioned earlier, Lacy returns to the school he grew up watching. During SEC Media Days, Lacy said he wanted to commit to Texas, but the Longhorns never gave him an opportunity. Now, he'll be on the opposing side with his family in the crowd. “It’s going to mean a lot, just coming back home. I don’t really hold anything against Texas," Lacy said. "But it’s a hometown game, so I’m excited to have all my family, friends there.” If the Rebels are going to pull off a massive road victory, they'll need Lacy to have another dominant game. picks.blurb: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week. picks.headline: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Reese, Dream win Game 3 Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut World Series preview Champions League results Fantasy Football Rankings Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:38 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will try to keep to momentum rolling as they enter their bye week after they host Vanderbilt under the lights on Saturday. Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 22, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky Football looks to keep climbing after Oklahoma win as Vanderbilt comes to Lexington. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. picks.headline: How No. 12 Kentucky football and Vanderbilt match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 21 of 28 passes for 158 yards and two touchdowns in the Wildcats’ 21-13 win at Oklahoma last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound transfer from Notre Dame has been a paragon of efficiency so far as a Wildcat. On the season, Minchey has completed 68.4% of his throws for 1,551 yards with 13 touchdowns vs. one interception . • Vanderbilt true freshman Jared Curtis is a player UK coach Will Stein sought to recruit while serving as Oregon offensive coordinator. “He’s very young,” Stein said of Curtis, “but in terms of the tangibles of the position, being able to throw it, arm talent, running strength, he is a prototype first-round-type talent.” A homegrown, 6-3, 230-pound Nashville product, Curtis is completing 62.7% of his throws for 1,242 yards and six touchdowns. Ball security has been an issue for the freshman QB, who has thrown seven interceptions and lost two fumbles. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky leading rusher CJ Baxter (484 yards, 5.6 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) sat out last week’s victory at Oklahoma with an undisclosed injury. In Baxter’s absence, third-year player Jason Patterson led UK with 38 yards on 12 carries vs. the Sooners. Former Oklahoma back Jovantae Barnes carried five times for 16 yards last week vs. his former team. • Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea deploys a two-man running back rotation. Senior Sedrick Alexander has run for 270 yards and five touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards a rush. The 5-9, 207-pound product of Austin, Texas, has also caught 11 passes for 94 yards and a score. Senior Makhilyn Young has rushed for 232 yards and two TDs and is averaging 4.2 yards a carry. A 5-10, 210-pound product of Midland, Texas, Young has caught 10 passes for 76 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby was named a Midseason Freshman All-American by On3 Sports this week. The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, leads UK with 34 catches and 436 receiving yards and is tied for the team lead with three touchdown receptions. Senior Nic Anderson made an acrobatic, juggling catch against Oklahoma — the team for whom he played as a freshman. Over the past three games, the 6-4, 205-pound Atlanta product has caught 13 passes. On the season, Anderson has 17 catches for 197 yards and a TD. • Vanderbilt senior Junior Sherrill is fourth in the SEC in receptions with 41. A 5-11, 200-pound Nashville product, Sherrill has 628 receiving yards and has caught four touchdown passes. In Vandy’s 45-17 strafing of UK last season, Sherrill caught eight passes for 115 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is putting together an All-SEC-caliber season. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School caught five passes for 38 yards and two touchdowns in last week’s win at Oklahoma. On the season, Rodriguez has 33 catches for 257 yards and three TDs. • A transfer from East Carolina who began his college career at Ole Miss, Vanderbilt’s Jayvontay Conner has 13 catches for 146 yards. Cole Spence has six receptions for 72 yards. In last season’s blowout of UK, Spence caught three passes for 48 yards. Offensive line • Kentucky left offensive tackle Lance Heard was named a First Team Mid-Season All-American this week by On3 Sports. A 6-6, 325-pound product of Bonita, Louisiana, Heard was recently ranked the 29th-best prospect for the 2027 NFL draft by CBSSports.com. • Vanderbilt “quick guard” Cade McConnell is the only returning starter along the offensive front from last season’s 10-3 team. A 6-5, 323-pound product of Choctaw, Oklahoma, McConnell began his college career at Minnesota. Center Lyndon Cooper logged 25 career starts at Pittsburgh and was considered a portal-recruiting coup for Vandy. Advantage: Kentucky Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace and tackle Tavion Gadson were disruptive forces for UK late in the win at Oklahoma. Humphrey-Grace, a 6-4, 271-pound senior from Cincinnati, was credited with 1.5 sacks and three quarterback hurries vs. the Sooners. It was Humphrey-Grace deflecting the ball off the throwing hand of Oklahoma QB John Mateer that set up the Ty Bryant interception that was the turning point in the game. Gadson, a 6-5, 303-pound junior from Savannah, Georgia, made eight tackles, 1.5 sacks and broke up a pass. “Those guys are really good players,” Will Stein said of Gadson and Humphrey-Grace. • At 6-7, 305 pounds, Vanderbilt tackle Issa Ouattara is an impactful presence in the interior of the Commodores’ defensive front. A product of Cologne, Germany, Ouattara has two sacks and three QB hurries so far in 2026. Edge Miles Capers leads Vandy with six tackles for loss and has two sacks, an interception and the forced fumble that set up Vanderbilt’s game-winning touchdown on the final play of a 35-31 victory over North Carolina State. • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey made a game-high 15 tackles at Oklahoma. WLB Bo Barnes was not far behind with 10 stops. It has been a season of starts and stops for fifth-year player Alex Afari . The 6-2, 227-pound Cincinnati product is a member of the high school class of 2022 that the NCAA has attempted to exclude from the new 5-for-5 eligibility model. Afari was eligible for UK’s first four games due to a ruling in Jefferson County Circuit Court. However, the NCAA won on appeal at the Kentucky Court of Appeals, making Afari ineligible for the South Carolina and LSU games. A subsequent ruling by the Jefferson County Circuit Court last week restored Afari’s eligibility prior to the Oklahoma contest. The legal back-and-forth “is frustrating for him and for us,” Will Stein said. “We just got to roll with the punches a little bit. It’s out of our control. It’s out of his control at the end of the day, and he’s responded appropriately.” • Vanderbilt WLB Nick Rinaldi is a stat stuffer. A 6-3, 240-pound product of Dover, Massachusetts, Rinaldi has made 42 tackles, 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks and has hurried the quarterback four times and broken up passes four times. MLB Bryan Longwell is second on the team with 50 tackles. Longwell had a TFL in Vandy’s rout of UK last season. Advantage : Vanderbilt Defensive backs • Kentucky senior safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell each had two interceptions in the win over Oklahoma. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound transfer from Florida, foiled a Sooners’ fake field goal with an interception in the end zone and later returned a pick of John Mateer 41 yards for the game’s final touchdown. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Frederick Douglass High School alumnus, set up Kentucky’s go-ahead TD with a 42-yard interception return, then sealed the Wildcats’ victory with a pick with 21 seconds left in the game. • Vanderbilt strong safety CJ Heard leads the Commodores in tackles with 52. A 5-11, 210-pound Atlanta product who began his college career at Florida Atlantic, Heard also has made four tackles for loss, three sacks, broken up five passes, forced two fumbles and intercepted a pass. Special teams • Kentucky has not had consistently stellar punting in 2026, but Wilson Berry played a big role in the win at Oklahoma. The Australian uncorked a 58-yard, rugby-style kick that backed OU up to its 4-yard line with 2:43 left in the game. On the season, Berry is averaging 44 yards on eight punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 8 of 11 on field goals in 2026 with a long make of 52 yards. • Vanderbilt punter Tyler Ebel is averaging 47 yards a kick and has pinned opponents inside their 20-yard line on 10 of 27 punts. Place-kicker Brock Taylor is 6 of 8 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 47 yards. For his college career, Taylor is 47 of 53 on field-goal tries with a long make of 57 yards. away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. away.blurb: Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt Injury Report: Sam Greene likely out; CJ Baxter set to play | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 22, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed CJ Baxter is set to make his return for the Kentucky Wildcats, but Same Greene appears unlikely to play. The big news is that standout linebacker Sam Greene is doubtful to play. Greene has played in every game this season after recovering from an ACL tear suffered toward the end of last season. Hopefully, this is not a significant issue and he’ll be able to return coming out of the Wildcats’ Week 9 bye. Running back CJ Baxter, who dressed for the Oklahoma game but was held out, is listed as probable, so he should play. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who left Saturday’s win in Norman late due to an injury, is listed as questionable, so there’s a 50-50 shot he plays for the time being. Linebacker Tavion Wallace, who’s missed the last three games, tweeted on Wednesday that he’d returned to practice, so that could be a boost to a position that’s been thin. Wallace is officially listed as probable. Fellow linebacker Antawn Smith, who was injured at South Carolina and missed the last two games, has been ruled out for this week. Cornerback Grant Grayton remains out. Cornerback Jaden Smith, who was also injured at South Carolina and hasn’t played since, has been ruled out. Defensive tackle Kalen Edwards is probable. Defensive end Tyler Thomas is questionable. Finally, long-snapper Cole Marszalek is listed as doubtful to play. For Vanderbilt, starting cornerback Cayden Daniels is probable. Backup defensive end Brian Allen Jr. is listed as out. Backup defensive end Haydon Brey is probable. Backup linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful to play. Backup safeties Dontae Carter and Devin Chandler are listed as questionable. Backup guard Mitchell Smith is probable. away.headline: Who Vanderbilt Football's Backup Quarterback is With Blaze Berlowitz Injury
away.blurb: Vanderbilt likely did not envision either Muschamp or Elliott being the No. 2 quarterback at any point this season. The only way that would happen would be in the case of an injury to Curtis or Berlowitz. Tuesday, Lea announced that Berlowitz is out for about a month with a broken collarbone. "They both have the ability to go out and operate. Both represent the program, both have the confidence of their teammates, both had really good attempts for the starting job. So there's a lot of faith and confidence in what those guys bring," Lea said. Who Vanderbilt Football's Backup Quarterback is With Blaze Berlowitz Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Ant spoils Giannis' Heat debut Vanderbilt quarterback Whit Muschamp (10) runs against Vanderbilt linebacker Daniel Vollmer Jr. (44) and linebacker Luke D'Alise (43) during Vanderbilt Football's Black and Gold Spring Game in FirstBank Stadium at Vanderbilt University Saturday, April 18, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Graham Baakko Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:05 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads NASHVILLE - Vanderbilt football head coach Clark Lea has always expressed confidence in every one of his players, including in his quarterback room. When the quarterback competition began in the offseason, Lea made sure to say it was a four-way competition. Ultimately, he narrowed the competition down between Jared Curtis and Blaze Berlowitz fighting for the starting spot while Whit Muschamp and Jack Elliott fought for the No. 3 spot in the room. With Curtis entering his second game back in the lineup after missing the Georgia game with a knee bruise injury, Muschamp and Elliott will be up next on the depth chart for the next month. The depth chart lists the backup spot as Muschamp or Elliott. So who would go into the game first if Curtis were to get hurt again this season? "Whit would be the first in," Lea said. "But there's a real world where we would see both of them. And those guys are excellent. I mean, I can't say enough good things about them." Both Muschamp and Elliott appeared in Vanderbilt's trip to Athens a couple of weeks ago. Elliott was in the game for one snap, where he took a snap and ran a quarterback draw on the play. Muschamp entered the game on Vanderbilt's final drive, where he completed two passes for a total of 18 yards. Both fared well for the Commodores in fall camp. Muschamp especially had a quietly good camp that gave the impression that he was closer to the No. 2 spot than he was being the No. 4 in the quarterback room. Ideally, Vanderbilt would prefer to not see another Curtis injury in the coming weeks. But if that were to happen again by chance, Lea feels confident and has belief in both Muschamp and Elliott to run the offense. Linebacker Grant Grayton is once again listed as out for Saturday's game. Will Stein does not expect it to be a season-long issue. “Not expected to be a season thing, so I'm hoping over the next few weeks we can get him back." The Wildcats will likely get CJ Baxter back ahead of Saturday's matchup, as he is listed as probable, along with linebacker Tavion Wallace. Kentucky football has been pretty banged up on the defensive end lately and were also without starting running back CJ Baxter this past Saturday against Oklahoma. After picking up a gritty win down in Norman, the Wildcats will be taking on a Vandy team that is winless in the SEC through four games, but one that Kentucky can't overlook. As the Wildcats continue to pop up in many playoff projections after yet another win, every single day becomes important if they want to capitalize on a historic start through seven games. Ahead of the matchup with Vandy, here is what the injury report looks like. Earlier this week, Stein made sure his players and fans know to not underestimate what Vandy can do. He isn't paying attention to that 3-4 record next to their name. "I don't think any of us in this room or this organization need to be fooled by any type of record. Last time I checked, (Vandy) embarrassed Kentucky last year and so we know what they are able to do in all three phases." Vandy also features one of the best wide receivers in the country, who is 11th nationally in receiving yards and a massive focal point in how they find success on offense. That, along with Kentucky needing to continue winning to keep their playoff hopes alive are the stories entering this one. The Wildcats can't afford a slip up ahead of a tough stretch to end the season. They'll be facing Vandy mostly healthy on Saturday. You can be mad at the officials for a bunch of bad or missed calls; you can shout at the offense for only scoring seven points; at Colton Joseph for only managing 66 passing yards; or even at the defense for being miserable on third downs. But wallow for a bit, reset, pick yourself up, and let's look at the upcoming game on Saturday. The Badgers get another primetime game on NBC against another Los Angeles school. There is a major difference between the two odds... the over/under looks a lot different. Wisconsin vs. UCLA was at low odds around 43.5, but now it's getting higher. You can basically flip that for Wisconsin, whose defense has been pretty spectacular this season, especially when it comes to scoring defense. home.blurb: Whether he just wasn’t quite ready or the Wisconsin staff wanted to play it safe, he stayed out against the Bruins, with more than half a season left. Stylz Blackmon, who had been playing right guard, moved to center to replace Kawecki, while PJ Wilkins slotted into guard. Now, Kawecki has been upgraded to ‘Probable’ ahead of the Badgers’ matchup with the Trojans. Kawecki’s return would be a nice boost for the offensive line that struggled mightily against UCLA last week. A pair of starters are ‘questionable’ for Saturday Two starters popped up on the report this week that we didn’t expect. Wide receiver Malachi Coleman and cornerback Javan Robinson are both listed as ‘questionable’ for Saturday. RB Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ The Badgers got Abu Sama back off the injury report last week, but injuries remain at the position. After missing last week’s game against UCLA, Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ for this week’s game. Palmer has received only a handful of carries this season, but he has been a constant presence on special teams and the team’s primary kick returner, returning six kicks for an average of 28.2 yards per return. Christian Borman Oct 22, 2026 Share Wisconsin Badgers wide receiver Malachi Coleman. Photo credit: UW Athletics The Wisconsin football team has released its initial availability report ahead of its matchup with USC this Saturday evening. Some players are trending in the right direction after missing time, but a couple of names on the report weren’t expected. Here’s where things stand three days ahead of the matchup with the Trojans. Austin Kawecki is trending in the right direction Starting center Austin Kawecki left in the middle of the Badgers’ game with Michigan State in Week 5. With a bye week to rest, there was hope he would be back for the Badgers’ road game against UCLA in Week 7. Javan Robinson has been the most consistent cornerback for the Badgers this season. If he misses the game, it would be a massive blow to the defense, especially in a week when they face one of the best passing quarterbacks in the country, Jordan Maiava. On top of that, the cornerback depth has already taken a hit this year after Cai Bates was lost for the season with a knee injury early in the year. Losing Coleman wouldn’t be ideal, either. But the passing attack for the Badgers has been inconsistent, and even after his breakout game against Notre Dame in Week 1, he hasn’t been the force we all hoped he’d be. Fortunately for the Badgers, they just got Jaylon Domingeaux back from injury last week and caught a pair of passes, so there is at least some more depth at receiver. home.headline: New Mexico linebacker Jaxton Eck out for 'a while' after suffering shoulder injury
home.blurb: Multiple Lobos listed as out or questionable for Saturday's game against Hawaii UNM’s Jaxton Eck (6) gets ready for the next play during a scrimmage at University Stadium in Albuquerque NM on August 15, 2026. Mike Sandoval/Journal Sean Reider Sean Reider Journal Staff Writer Published October 15, 2026 - 12:01 p.m. Modified October 15, 2026 - 2:34 p.m. New Mexico linebacker Jaxton Eck will be out for “a while” after breaking a bone in his shoulder, head coach Jason Eck told the Journal on Thursday. The 6-foot-1, 228-pound senior did not practice this week and was observed with his arm in a sling before he was ruled out for Saturday’s game at Hawaii. Jason Eck said the preseason Mountain West Defensive Player of the Year’s bone break is in the same shoulder he hurt in the Rate Bowl on Dec. 27. Eck added that he does not believe Jaxton’s injury is season-ending, but expects him to miss an extended period of time. His designation was first released via an initial availability report from the Mountain West on Thursday, one that saw multiple key Lobos listed as out or questionable ahead of Saturday’s game. Late to seeing this: LB Jaxton Eck and CB Frankie Edwards III are OUT for Saturday’s game. WR Massiah Mingo and RB Kiefer Sibley are also questionable. https://t.co/5jqZVKeiZ5 Only one Lobo was newly ruled out for the rest of the season on the initial report: backup linebacker Nick Wheeler, who Eck said suffered a torn ACL. Without Jaxton and Wheeler, UNM is expected to rely on linebackers Mercury Swaim and Clay Martineau for the near future. Starting cornerback Frankie Edwards III (9 total tackles) has also been ruled out for Saturday’s game, per the league’s availability report. Eck said the 5-10, 178-pound junior suffered a concussion, and expects him to return as soon as next week. Wide receiver Massiah Mingo (ankle) and running back Kiefer Sibley (shoulder) are questionable for Saturday’s game, per the availability report. A 5-9, 170-pound freshman, Mingo has caught five passes for 56 yards; Sibley has rushed for 205 yards, the second-best mark on the team.
